title: Protons, Neutrons and Electrons
short: The number of protons, the atomic number, decides which element an atom is.
trouble: Students think the number of neutrons or electrons decides the element.

blocks.html: How We Learned What Atoms Are found three kinds of particles inside atoms. You met charges in Electric Charge; here we pin down what each particle carries and which number decides what an atom is.

blocks.html: The number of protons, the atomic number $Z$, decides which element an atom is. Every carbon atom has 6 protons; every atom with 6 protons is carbon. A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, so its charges cancel.

Chemistry happens through electrons, but the electrons are arranged by the pull of the nucleus, and that pull comes from the protons. Change the number of neutrons and the nucleus gets heavier, but its charge, and so the electrons and the chemistry, stay nearly the same. Change the number of electrons and you get an ion of the same element, which can gain its electrons back. Only a change in the number of protons makes a different element, and that takes a nuclear reaction, not a chemical one.

blocks.cap: Build an atom: add or remove protons, neutrons and electrons. Only the proton count changes the element’s name.

blocks.title: Using the atomic number
blocks.q: Sulfur has atomic number 16. How many protons and electrons does a neutral sulfur atom have?

blocks.title: Naming the element
blocks.q: An atom has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons. What is it?
steps: Only the 11 protons matter for the name: element 11 is sodium, Na.
11 electrons balance 11 protons, so it is a neutral sodium atom.

blocks.html: Thinking the number of neutrons or electrons decides the element. An atom with 6 protons and 8 neutrons is still carbon (carbon-14), and a sodium atom that loses an electron is still sodium (a sodium ion). Check: look only at the protons, the atomic number on the periodic table.
Build atoms yourself and watch the element change only when you add or remove a proton: Build an Atom.
